newsitem.title: USA: HFS net income more than doubles in quarter.
newsitem.headline: HFS net income more than doubles in quarter.

text.p: HFS Inc., a day after closing its merger with PHH Corp., said Thursday the combined company's profits more than doubled as it continued to change from a pure hotel franchisor into a real estate and travel-related firm.
Net income soared 111 percent to $91.1 million, or 52 cents, from $43.3 million, or 29 cents, for first quarter last year. Combined revenues rose 88 percent to $527 million from $280 million.
Excluding PHH, HFS's profits rose 158 percent to $59 million, or 41 cents a share, or 20 cents a share, from $23 million. Revenue jumped 179 percent to $348 million from $125 million.
HFS and PHH agreed in November to merge in a $1.7 billion stock deal. PHH, based in Hunt Valley, Md., delivers vehicle leasing and fleet management services, as well as employee relocation services.
Henry Silverman, chairman of the Parsippany, N.J.-based company, said the company has introduced a number of cross marketing programmes.
For example, a relocating employee can be served by HFS's affiliated Century 21 real estate brokers, Days Inn, Ramada, Travelodge and Howard Johnson hotels, and Avis Inc. rental car unit, it said.
HFS is the largest franchisor of hotels and rental cars, the leading provider of vacation timeshare exchanges and is the second largest vehicle management company worldwide.
HFS's stock rose 50 cents to $59.75 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
